items.new_note: Matthew 10:6 — *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* Acts 29:2 — *For he had heard in Phoenicia that certain of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), about the time of the Assyrian captivity, had escaped by sea to "the isles afar off," as spoken by the prophet, and called by the Romans, Britain.* (Acts 29:2) Yahusha (Jesus) sent his disciples to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and this manuscript tells of Paul going after the same sheep. It says some of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) had escaped by sea about the time of the Assyrian captivity, which puts the lost sheep of Matthew 10:6 among the scattered of that captivity, far from the land. The manuscript has Paul setting out for Spain and Britain because he had heard where they went.
items.new_member_note: Acts 29:2 — *certain of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), about the time of the Assyrian captivity, had escaped by sea to "the isles afar off,"* This is the manuscript's reason for Paul's journey to Spain and Britain, following the lost sheep of Matthew 10:6 to where they were scattered.
items.flag: Isaiah 49:1 / Jeremiah 31:10 not quoted: their texts are not in the packet and the brief says quote them in full if used. Old note's wording about the Matthew 10 commission kept in plain prose.

items.new_note: Matthew 10:6 — *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* Acts 29:3 — *And Yahuah (Lord) commanded the gospel to be preached far hence to the Gentiles, and to the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Acts 29:3) The manuscript puts into Paul's commission the very words Yahusha (Jesus) spoke to his disciples, the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel), and sends him far hence with them. It sets the Gentiles beside those sheep, and since the sheep were scattered among the nations, the Gentiles named here may well be that same scattered flock living as Gentiles. So the manuscript carries the commission of Matthew 10:6 out of Galilee to wherever the scattered went.
items.new_member_note: Acts 29:3 — *Yahuah (Lord) commanded the gospel to be preached far hence to the Gentiles, and to the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel).* The manuscript carries the commission of Matthew 10:6 and Matthew 15:24 out to the far places where the scattered flock was driven.

items.new_note: Matthew 10:23 — *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* Acts 29:13 — *And it came to pass that certain of the Druids came unto Paul privately, and showed by their rites and ceremonies they were descended from the Yahudim (Jews) which escaped from bondage in the land of Egypt, and the apostle believed these things, and he gave them the kiss of peace.* (Acts 29:13) Yahusha (Jesus) told his disciples they would not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) before the Son of Adam came, so the search for Yashar'el (Israel) was meant to outlast them. The manuscript tells of Paul finding, in Britain, men whose rites and ceremonies pointed back to the exodus from Egypt, and of his giving them the kiss of peace. It is a disputed witness, but it shows the scattered children being found where they were driven, which is what Matthew 10:23 leaves still to be done.
items.new_member_note: Acts 29:13 — *certain of the Druids came unto Paul privately, and showed by their rites and ceremonies they were descended from the Yahudim (Jews) which escaped from bondage in the land of Egypt.* The manuscript has Paul finding the scattered children in Britain, where Matthew 10:23 says the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) are not yet fully gone over.

items.new_note: 1 Corinthians 15:36 — *Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die.* Paul's seed that is not quickened unless it dies is the picture Clement draws of the sower: the seeds fall into the earth dry and bare and decay, and then the Master's providence raises them up and they bear fruit (1 Clement 1:24).
